articles.title: What is Server-Side Rendering (SSR)?
articles.content: Server-Side Rendering (SSR) is a technique used in web development to improve the performance and search engine optimization (SEO) of web applications. In SSR, the HTML content of a page is generated on the server rather than in the browser. This approach contrasts with client-side rendering (CSR), where the browser generates the HTML content after downloading JavaScript, CSS, and other resources.

articles.title: Introduction to Redux: State Management for React
articles.content: In modern web development, managing state in complex applications can become tricky. As your app grows, the flow of data between components can become difficult to maintain, leading to bugs, performance issues, and a tangled codebase. This is where Redux comes in — a predictable state container for JavaScript applications, often used with React to manage the state of an app in a consistent and scalable way.

articles.title: Redux vs. Context API: Which One to Use and When?
articles.content: When building React applications, one of the fundamental challenges is managing state — especially in larger applications where multiple components need access to shared data. In this context, React Context API and Redux are two popular solutions for managing state across components. While both are used to manage global state, they have distinct differences in terms of usage, scalability, and complexity.

articles.content: React has long been a powerful library for building user interfaces, and over the years, it has evolved to provide developers with more efficient ways of rendering, updating, and managing data in their applications. Two of the most exciting innovations in React are Suspense and Concurrent Mode. These features, still relatively new and evolving, promise to revolutionize the way we build and optimize React applications, especially when it comes to performance, user experience, and responsiveness.

articles.title: How to Build a Custom React Hook: Best Practices and Real-World Examples
articles.content: React's hook system has revolutionized how developers manage state and side effects in functional components. While React provides a variety of built-in hooks like useState, useEffect, and useContext, the real power comes from custom hooks. Custom hooks allow you to extract and reuse logic across components, keeping your code clean, modular, and maintainable.

When paired with React, a powerful JavaScript library for building user interfaces, a design system can significantly enhance the speed and consistency of development while ensuring a smooth user experience across different platforms.

articles.content: Animations are more than just eye candy — they play a crucial role in enhancing the user experience (UX) by making applications feel more interactive, fluid, and polished. Whether it’s for transitions, loading states, or subtle visual feedback, animations can greatly improve how users perceive your apps performance and usability.

articles.content: In the fast-paced world of web development, efficiency and consistency are paramount.
